correctness.rationale: Exact KG(5,2) ten-vertex path enumeration produces 120 states; application of both-end backbites produces 240 undirected edges, all degree four. The 120 S5 relabellings of one stated path are distinct and give a regular graph action, whose four reference neighbors yield the exact inverse-closed Cayley generators. BFS on all S5 words gives seven shells totaling 120 and 11 antipodes at distance six. An independent GP(5,2) edge-mask enumeration yields the same states, edges and all-source shell profile. The graph-isomorphism and path-edge-flip equivalence are explicitly proved; finite exhaustive verification is fully sufficient for this fixed graph.

value.rationale: A canonical smallest cubic non-Hamiltonian graph produces a natural finite state space of spanning paths. The move is the classical Pósa/backbite step, and recent general connectivity theorems leave this sparse graph uncovered. The theorem gives a nontrivial structural surprise (the graph is non-Cayley, while its entire path rotation graph is a regular Cayley graph on S5), an explicit four-generator model, exact finite orbit count and sharp diameter six. This is a motivated complete reconfiguration classification rather than a textbook identity or routine renamed invariant.
